FieldReference.description: A field reference binds a field identity to its declaring State.

Flow.description:
A state machine bound to one player or global integer State field.

The shared Rust/portable lifecycle runs automatic State maintenance, then
flows, then authored module tick actions. Writes from a module's tick body
therefore affect flow selection on the following cycle. Within a flow,
transitions run before tick hooks, and later hooks observe earlier writes.

hooks.description:
Hooks retain authored order. Tick hooks observe state changes made by
earlier hooks in the same cycle; raw score writes bypass enter/exit hooks.

id.description: Stable identity owning generated private helpers and interval counters.

state.description:
The field's owning scope determines execution: each player or one server
invocation for global State. Lifecycle initializes its declared default.

transitions.description:
At most one transition executes per cycle. Equal-priority guards retain
declaration order; identical guards targeting different states conflict.

FlowHook.description: A named function invoked at a state-machine lifecycle point.

cadence.description:
Tick hooks count matching cycles, including the entering cycle. Counters
reset when a cycle observes another phase. Range: 1 through i32::MAX.
Enter and exit hooks require the default value of one.

function.description: Inherits the flow's player or server execution context.

phase.description: Enter/exit hooks run only on flow-owned transitions.

FlowHookPhase.description: The state-machine lifecycle point that invokes a hook.

FlowTransition.description: One guarded transition between integer phases.

from.description: Required current phase; arbitrary signed integer encodings are supported.

priority.description: Higher priorities first; ties retain declaration order.

to.description:
Exact destination phase; must differ from the source and satisfy any
bounds on the owning State field.

when.description: No guard means unconditional once the source phase is selected.

bounds.description:
Inclusive bounds applied by score assignment and addition. Initialization
preserves the declared default, matching Rust State lifecycle semantics.
The minimum must not exceed the maximum. Addition uses Minecraft's i32
arithmetic before clamping; these bounds do not prevent overflow.

default.description:

supported. Reloading or re-entering a function preserves existing values.
